gqm.goal: Keep the Neovim configuration understandable and consistently validated for maintainers.
questions: Are Lua files formatted and free of configured language-server diagnostics?
Are repository text and configuration files free of known spelling errors?

measures.evidence: Command exit code and bounded diagnostic output
measures.limitations: Does not establish user-facing behavior or runtime compatibility.

factors.applicability: Tracked Lua and repository configuration files

gqm.goal: Avoid introducing configuration errors that prevent Neovim startup.
questions: Can the configuration be loaded in a headless Neovim process with isolated state?

measures.limitations: Does not exercise interactive UI behavior or every lazy-loaded plugin path.

gqm.goal: Prevent credentials or private data from being committed in editor configuration.
questions: Does the configuration introduce a concrete secret exposure path?

measures.evidence: Finding with source location, attack precondition, and impact
measures.limitations: Semantic review is not a proof that no undiscovered vulnerability exists.

factors.applicability: Configuration, plugin, and external-command integration code

analysis_skills.name: requirements-review
analysis_skills.evidence: Reviewed repository scope; no separate product requirements document exists.

analysis_skills.name: architecture-review
analysis_skills.evidence: Configuration is organized by startup, LSP, commands, and plugin groups; no new dependency boundary was introduced by the .gitignore/lint changes.

analysis_skills.name: change-impact-review
analysis_skills.evidence: Checked Makefile consumers, Lua configuration files, ignored/generated paths, and startup entrypoint; no downstream API or persistence consumer was found.

analysis_skills.name: security-review
analysis_skills.evidence: Reviewed configuration and shell-command integration for secret exposure, unsafe path handling, and external command risks; no concrete finding in the assessed scope.

analysis_skills.name: whitebox-risk-based-test
analysis_skills.evidence: Risk analysis covered startup loading, Lua diagnostics, Makefile tool installation, and generated tool paths; make lint passed.

mechanical_checks.when: for changes to Lua, Makefile, or repository configuration

must_quality.rule: Requested behavior is satisfied and demonstrated by tests or evidence
Existing supported behavior is not unintentionally broken
Repository-local guidance and public contracts are respected
No critical security defect is introduced

performance_quality.rule: Keep responsibilities, names, and tests easy to evolve

critical_defects: Data loss, corruption, or unsafe migration
Required behavior missing or public API broken without approval
assumptions: LuaLS is installed with make install-lua-language-server when it is not already available.
The LuaLS warning-level check is the repository's current lint policy; runtime behavior still requires a headless Neovim check.
dprint remains unavailable in the restricted environment when its plugin cache is not writable; this is not treated as a passing check.
